diagnostic_evidence.quote: The real-valued spherical harmonics form an orthonormal basis of $L^2(\S^2)$.

issues.failure_explanation: As written, for every m<0 the function is just the scalar multiple |m|φ of φ. For fixed ℓ≥1 these negative-m modes are linearly dependent, and Δ(|m|φ)=0 while -ℓ(ℓ+1)|m|φ≠0, so the immediately following eigenvalue identity and the asserted orthonormal basis are false for the defined family.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Replace the m<0 branch by the standard real spherical harmonic complementary branch: the associated-Legendre/factorial-normalized P_{ℓ,|m|}(cos θ) times cos(|m|φ), with sign convention chosen consistently with the m>0 branch; then the eigenvalue identity and orthonormality are restored.
issues.overall_effect: Taken literally, the spherical-harmonic basis and eigenfunction property used in the KL expansion, the mild solution, and all spectral truncations are unreliable until the m<0 branch is replaced by the standard complementary associated-Legendre spherical harmonic.
issues.title: negative-order spherical harmonics are not the complementary Legendre eigenfunctions
issues.why_classification: The correction is local and definitional; with the standard branch every later spectral expansion and eigenvalue computation survives unchanged.

issues.failure_explanation: For ℓ=0 the semigroup factor is 1, so the noise mean contribution to the stochastic convolution is t mean_{0,0}. If mean_{0,0}≠0, then ‖X(t)‖_{L^p(H^ρ)} grows at least linearly in t, whereas the stated right-hand side is bounded in t apart from the initial-data singular factor. The proof's key estimate also bounds var_{0,0}t+(mean_{0,0}t)^2 by (3/2)(var_{0,0}+mean_{0,0}^2), which is false for large t.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Add the mean contribution to the bound, e.g. a term of order t‖mean‖_{L^p(H^ρ)} (with the zero-mode integral estimated as t rather than 1), or explicitly restrict the proposition to centered noise; fixed-time applications used later then survive.
issues.overall_effect: The time-uniform regularity estimate in Proposition prop:regul is not valid for the explicitly allowed non-centered Lévy case; uses of that proposition to justify test-function classes must be repaired by adding the mean contribution or by centering the noise.
issues.title: regularity bound ignores the non-centered zero-mode mean growth
issues.why_classification: A contained repair restores the finite-time regularity needed later, but the displayed uniform-in-time conclusion must be changed and the zero-mode mean estimate repaired.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: the processes $(L_{\ell,m})_{\ell,m}$ are assumed to be independent if $p>2$

issues.failure_explanation: The centered coefficient L_{ℓ,m}(s)-s mean_{ℓ,m} is generally a purely discontinuous Lévy martingale. The quadratic-variation-only Burkholder-Davis-Gundy bound is not valid for such martingales: for independent unit-jump compensated Poisson coefficients with intensities λ_{ℓm}=(2ℓ+1)^{-1}ℓ^{-2}, one has Λ=∑λ_{ℓm}<∞, so L∈L^4(H^0), but E‖∫_0^1 e^{Δ_{S^2}(1-s)}dL(s)‖_{H^1}^4 is at least a constant times ∑_{ℓm}(1+ℓ(ℓ+1))^2 λ_{ℓm}(1-e^{-4ℓ(ℓ+1)})/(4ℓ(ℓ+1)) ≥ c∑_{ℓ}1=∞. Thus η=0, ρ=1, p=4 satisfies ρ-η≤1 but the claimed conclusion fails; the jump term forces the stronger restriction ρ-η<2/p unless additional jump-moment assumptions are imposed.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: For p>2 in case ass1Reg, replace the quadratic-variation-only estimate by a Lévy-martingale moment estimate including the jump compensator, and restrict the range to ρ-η<2/p or impose the jump-moment control of Assumption ass:NoMeanLevyProcess; equivalently align this case with ass2Reg.
issues.overall_effect: The p>2 independent-Lévy branch of Proposition prop:regul is false in the stated range, and Corollary cor:added-1's first two settings inherit the defect for non-Gaussian p>2 test functions; the NoMean regime with ρ-η<2/p remains the valid template.
issues.title: p>2 independent Lévy case uses a continuous-martingale BDG bound and omits the jump term
issues.why_classification: The supported repair changes the hypothesis/range for a central regularity claim: independent jump Lévy noise no longer gives the full one-derivative L^p smoothing for p>2, which materially weakens the derived weak-convergence corollary for higher-order polynomial test functions.

issues.failure_explanation: The first component of E[X(t)]-E[X^{(κ)}(t)] has squared norm ∑_{ℓ>κ}e^{-2ℓ(ℓ+1)t}E[X^0_{ℓ,m}]^2, whose square root is bounded by e^{-(κ+1)^2t}‖E[X^0]‖, not by e^{-2(κ+1)^2t}‖E[X^0]‖. The intermediate line therefore claims a smaller initial-condition factor than the triangle estimate gives; the final corollary only needs the weaker e^{-(κ+1)^2t} factor.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: In the displayed triangle bound replace e^{-2(κ+1)^2t} by e^{-(κ+1)^2t}; no change to the corollary statement is needed.
issues.overall_effect: Only an intermediate inequality in the proof of Corollary L:SA2 is too strong; the stated corollary remains valid after weakening that line to the final exponential factor.
issues.title: mean-error proof uses a too-small exponential factor
issues.why_classification: This is a one-symbol exponent correction that preserves the stated rate and all downstream uses.

issues.failure_explanation: Assumption ass:StrongLevyProcess allows η=-1, but then min{(η+1)/2,1}=0 and min{η+1,1}=0, while Proposition prop:AuxExp is only stated for μ∈(0,1]. The same endpoint is needed for the variance term in Theorem Thm:ConvEM2. The constant-rate case β=0 is still recoverable because ℓ(ℓ+1)^{2μ-1}h^{2μ}=ℓ(ℓ+1)^{-1}(ℓ(ℓ+1)h)^{2μ}≤C_c^{2μ}ℓ(ℓ+1)^{-1}, and similarly ℓ(ℓ+1)^{μ-1}h^μ≤C_c^μℓ(ℓ+1)^{-1}.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Keep any fixed μ∈(0,1] and use ℓ(ℓ+1)h≤C_c to convert the μ-dependent powers into ℓ(ℓ+1)^{-1} for η=-1, or state prop:AuxExp also for μ=0; alternatively restrict these two estimates to η>-1.
issues.overall_effect: The strong and second-moment Euler-Maruyama estimates are not proven at the boundary η=-1 as written, although the β=0 conclusion is a constant bound and can be recovered by the stability factor rewrite or by extending prop:AuxExp to μ=0.
issues.title: Euler-Maruyama proofs invoke the exponential estimates at the endpoint μ=0
issues.why_classification: The endpoint has no rate content (β=0 is only a constant bound), and the stability-factor rewrite is a short local repair with no loss of advertised rates.
